section_title: How does daily teaching in Ephesus reach beyond the city?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 8 Then Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months, arguing persuasively about the kingdom of God. 9 But when some of them stubbornly refused to believe and publicly maligned the Way, Paul took his disciples and left the synagogue to conduct daily discussions in the lecture hall of Tyrannus. 10 This continued for two years, so that everyone who lived in the province of Asia, Jews and Greeks alike, heard the word of the Lord.

context_lines: Paul speaks boldly in the synagogue for three months, explaining and seeking to persuade his hearers about God’s kingdom. When some refuse to believe and publicly speak against the Way, he leaves with the disciples and continues daily discussions in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.

The teaching continues for two years, with the result that Jewish and Greek people throughout the province of Asia hear the Lord’s word. Asia here is a Roman province, rather than the whole modern continent. Luke describes the wide reach of the message without listing every journey or naming the founder of every church.

The move changes the place of instruction without ending the work. The regular teaching matters alongside the remarkable events that follow. Luke does not tell us the hall’s precise schedule or every detail of how it was made available.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly read this as persistent teaching that adapts when opposition closes one setting. The account values sustained explanation and the spread of the message through a wider region; it does not make a particular kind of meeting building essential to the mission.
god_plan_lines: Paul had earlier been prevented from speaking the word in Asia in [Acts 16:6](https://biblehub.com/bsb/acts/16.htm). Now the same region hears it widely. The earlier restraint was not a permanent rejection of its people. In the larger movement promised in [Acts 1:8](https://biblehub.com/bsb/acts/1.htm), God opens opportunities at different times, and steady teaching becomes a means by which the witness reaches beyond one gathering.
current_position_lines: We don't have a position on this passage yet. When our study reaches a conclusion the text supports, it will appear here.
